Winningest Hemi Cuda Ever: Totaled in 1970, Won 45 Races in Five Years, You Never Heard of It
85 photos
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce
What's the winningest Hemi Cuda ever? While American drag strips usually claim the most famous Plymouth muscle cars, the undisputed global champion actually conquered the most un-American race tracks ever. Literally, and figuratively. This 1970 Plymouth ‘Cuda 4-speed and its 426 Hemi triumphed in road racing in France in a way no other Mopar did. And it’s for sale.
We’re having a downpour of blue 1970 racing royalty over at Bring a Trailer, apparently. A few days ago, Carl Tasca’s 1970 Boss 429 drag car was listed, sporting Richard Petty’s Boss 429 V8. And now, it’s Henri Chemin’s former champion E-body’s turn to heat up the bidding wars, after its glorious triumphs on the winding circuits and mountain climbs of Europe, more than 50 years ago.
Meet chassis BS23R0B249759, the factory-backed 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda 4-speed campaigned by Ecurie Chrysler, Ma’ Mopar’s French division. Between 1970 and 1974, this extraordinary machine captured 45 documented Group 1 victories across fierce European road races and grueling French Alpine hillclimbs.
Understanding how a heavy Detroit bruiser dominated European motorsport requires a bit motoring archivistic shoveling. Launched in 1964 on the compact A-body platform shared with the economical Valiant, the early Barracuda featured a distinctive wraparound glass fastback and an optional 273-cubic-inch V8.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce A redesigned second generation arrived in 1967 with dedicated sheet metal, offering notchback, fastback, and convertible bodies paired with optional 340-cubic-inch, 383-cubic-inch, and 440-cubic-inch performance engines.
The legend of the Hemi Barracuda began in 1968 when Chrysler stuffed its 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8 into 50 lightweight A-body fastbacks strictly for Super Stock drag racing. Everything changed for the 1970 model year when Plymouth abandoned the A-body architecture for the wider, lower E-body platform shared with the Dodge Challenger. The bigger body came about precisely to give the big-blocks proper accommodation.
The performance-oriented 'Cuda trim finally brought the 425-horsepower 7.0-liter Hemi V8 to regular public showroom floors across America. Equipped with a functional Shaker hood scoop, heavy-duty suspension, and dual 4-barrel Carter AFB carburetors, the E-body Hemi 'Cuda became the ultimate symbol of raw American muscle.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce High insurance premiums and steep sticker prices kept production numbers remarkably low overall. Plymouth built just 652 Hemi 'Cuda hardtops and 14 convertibles for 1970, followed by 108 hardtops and 7 convertibles in 1971 before tightening emissions regulations put down the legendary engine.
In North American motorsport, E-body Mopars waged war on two major fronts during 1970. When the National Hot Rod Association introduced its heads-up Pro Stock category for the 1970 season, legendary drag racing duo Ronnie Sox and Buddy Martin campaigned a 4-speed Hemi 'Cuda that dominated quarter-mile drag strips across 1970 and 1971.
Simultaneously, Chrysler targeted road racing by officially entering the prestigious Sports Car Club of America Trans-Am Championship. Chrysler commissioned Dan Gurney and his All American Racers team to build three factory Plymouth Barracudas for the 1970 Trans-Am season alongside the sister Dodge Challenge r T/A program.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce Driven by Gurney and young teammate Swede Savage, those acid-dipped racers used destroked 303.8-cubic-inch V8 engines producing 450 horsepower, titanium suspension upright components, and computer-designed roll cages, while spawning 2,724 street-legal AAR 'Cuda homologation models powered by 340-cubic-inch Six Pack V8 engines.
While American teams battled unsuccessfully in Trans-Am, an even more remarkable E-body racing story unfolded across the Atlantic Ocean in France. Having steadily acquired shares in French automaker Simca since 1958, Chrysler formalized its Chrysler France subsidiary in 1970, which also encompassed Matra Automobiles.
Competition director Henri Chemin, who previously led Ford France's racing and public relations programs, launched Ecurie Chrysler France and ordered four Plymouth 'Cudas for spirited European competition.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce The centerpiece of that French fleet was chassis BS23R0B249759, a 1970 Hemi 'Cuda built to export specifications in Alpine White over black vinyl bucket seats with the A33 Track Pak, an A833 4-speed manual transmission, and a 3.54:1 axle. Registered under French license plate 6752 WK 75, the coupe received crucial chassis tuning from Matra race engineers, who realigned the front brake calipers, adjusted ballast, and relocated dual batteries in the trunk.
Deciphering the original fender tag reveals how Hamtramck assembly line 1 configured this Plymouth 'Cuda 2-door hardtop. Finished in Alpine White paint over high-grade black vinyl trim with full door panels, it paired the 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8 and 4-speed manual transmission with the A33 Track Pak and 26-inch radiator.
Interior appointments included bucket seats, a woodgrain console, power windows, and a Rallye cluster with a tachometer and a 150-mph speedo (quite strange, for an export to Europe car). Additional factory equipment comprised power brakes, a Shaker sport hood with tie-down pins, fender turn signals, a right-hand racing mirror, dual exhaust with chrome tips, and drip rail, wide sill, and rear deck moldings throughout the exterior body.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce Most intriguing is the rare N31 code, listed on the broadcast sheet under “N” engine accessories as optional compression ratio. Instead of a bespoke ratio, N31 always lowered compression to roughly 8.0:1 to 8.5:1 for domestic government or fleet vehicles avoiding costly premium fuel. On this export Hemi 'Cuda, it accommodated lower-octane European gasoline through reduced compression, re-jetted carburetors, and a specifically recurved ignition distributor.
Chemin immediately excelled in 1970, winning nine events at venues including Autun and Turckheim to secure Ecurie Chrysler France's first circuit championship. Disaster struck on August 23, 1970, at the Brides-Méribel hillclimb when power steering failure sent Chemin plunging 65 feet into a steep wooded ravine.
With the shell ruined, mechanics transferred the original engine, transmission, driveline, dashboard, and gauges into a replacement body (promptly sourced from a 440-Six-Barrel car bought alongside the Hemi car), returning to competition the following month. I don’t know the undersides and nuances of French automobile governing bodies, but the rebodied pony car kept the VIN from the original shell, although that had been deemed a total loss.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce Rebuilt and unstoppable, the Plymouth achieved its peak in 1971, earning 16 victories at circuits including Albi, Montlhéry, Magny-Cours, and Paul Ricard. When the original 426-cubic-inch Hemi failed mid-season, mechanics installed the engine from a 1971 team car, chassis BS23R1B215686. Chemin added 7 wins in 1972 for circuit and hillclimb titles, before Jean-François Mas scored 12 victories in 1973 and privateer Jean-Claude Géral won a hillclimb at Charnizay in 1974.
After retiring from competition, the Equipe Alméras Frères team sold the ' Cuda in 1976 to a Lyon buyer who painted it white and kept it until 2007. The caretaker who got it stored the racer in a barn for five years until the current owner bought it in 2012. Imported to America, the coupe underwent a comprehensive restoration by Redline Restorations in Bridgeport, Connecticut, conducted in direct consultation with Henri Chemin.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/1600veloce Refinished in its 1971 French-Blue-and-white livery with Shell and Cibie graphics, the coupe features 15-inch steel wheels, an 8.75-inch axle, a Hurst pistol-grip shifter, a 150-mph speedometer, and an 8,000-rpm tachometer. In 2013, the owner recovered the original matching-numbers 0B249759 engine block after decades in France and Canada. Honored at Greenwich and Hershey, the restored Plymouth returned to France in 2014 so Chemin could lap historic Circuit Paul Ricard again.
Now, this historic 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda is offered for sale at no reserve on Bring a Trailer by New York dealer 1600Veloce, complete with its spare original engine block, period scrapbooks, FIVA identity card, and upcoming display at Retromobile New York. As collectors pursue this 45-time race winner, the current bid stands at $110,000 with 10 days left on the auction clock. Is it going to go into seven figures?
Via // Bring A Trailer

Tuned BMW 7 Series Comes With a Carbon Makeover, Looks Like a Massive Sports Sedan
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign
It’s been more than half a year since BMW pulled the wraps off the latest iteration 7 Series , and now the flagship sedan is getting some aftermarket attention courtesy of Larte Design.
What would that be, you ask? Well, by touching it with its tuning stick, of course, which it just did. Or plans to do, because these are nothing more than mere renderings of the tuned project, yet unlike the usual digital illustrations that cross our screens, these actually preview something that is right around the corner. So, if you dig the design and plan to make your modern-day 7er look like this, then you know what to do, don’t you?
But speaking of the design, what is new? Well, unlike some other tuning jobs from different companies, which tend to keep things extremely discreet, Larte Design is not famously known for its restrained projects. And they weren’t going to make an exception for the latest iteration of the BMW 7 Series, which is a facelift of the G70 that hit the assembly line back in mid-2022, in case you forgot, and comes to life in Germany and in Southeast Asia.
The front hood has clearly come from the tuner’s portfolio. It features a pair of large vents in the middle, and two smaller ones on each side, and it is joined by a chunkier-looking splitter attached to the OEM bumper. These parts have been made of carbon fiber, and so have the side skirt attachments, the wing added on the trunk lid, and the large diffuser at the rear, which features a pair of integrated brake lights in the middle.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Do you know that no (visual) tuning job would be complete these days without a set of aftermarket wheels? Well, this BMW 7 Series also checks this box. Due to their multi-spoke design, the alloys remind us of Alpina’s creations, and that is definitely a compliment, though it is worth mentioning that Alpina’s wheels are better looking than these ones, this writer thinks.
The alloys have a black finish, sport a larger diameter than the stock ones, and had to be shod in rubber band tires in order to fit below the arches. The 7er in question appears to sit closer to the ground, so some suspension tweaks are part of the virtual (for now) makeover, and the car wears a red paint finish on the lower parts of the body, and a black look on the upper sections, whereas the add-ons mentioned above have a dry carbon look.
With Larte Design’s makeover, the latest iteration BMW 7 Series definitely looks a lot more aggressive than the standard one, but does this look suit it? You be the judge of that, and while you’re at it, you should know that the extras can also be painted black for a more discreet look. Speaking of painting, besides red, the tuner’s website also shows the car in other colors, including green, blue, gray, white, and so on.
One thing that the website, nor the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, do not reveal is how much it will cost you in order to make your modern-day BMW 7 Series look like this. Therefore, if you really must go for this look, then you should contact the tuner and discuss the details. By the way, this body kit has been especially developed for the LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) iteration, which is Bimmer slang for facelift, version of the G70 7er.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign According to Larte Design , every component of the body kit fits the factory mounting points, so the OEM-level fitment is guaranteed. This means that the installation should be a walk in the park, just like restoring the car back to its original condition. The tuner will ship the bundle worldwide, but realistically speaking, would you really want your 7er to look like this?
Before you decide whether you think it is worth it or not, we will remind you that the 2027 BMW 7 Series starts at $99,800 in the United States of America for the base 740, which uses a 394-horsepower 3-liter twin-turbocharged straight-six engine. The xDrive all-wheel drive system is a $3,000 optional extra in this case, and drops the 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) from 5.2 to 4.9 seconds, whereas the average fuel consumption is still rated at 30 mpg (7.8 l/100 km).
The latest BMW 7 Series features an updated front fascia and a new back end. The cockpit, meanwhile, looks basically the same as the ones belonging to other modern-day Bimmers, including the new X5, 3 Series, i3, etc. It is home to the Panoramic iDrive, a free-floating infotainment system, standard passenger display, a quirky-looking steering wheel with a four-spoke design, and a few other bits and bobs. View this post on Instagram A post shared by LARTE DESIGN | BODY KITS | WHEELS | AUTO DESIGN (@lartedesign)

The Hyundai Ioniq 6 N Isn't Just a 5 N Copy in a Sedan Body, Here's Why Its Better
30 photos
Photo: Naveed Hussain / autoevolution
Hyundai's N division has long been celebrated by petrolheads worldwide, so it's little wonder we fell in love with the IONIQ 5 N when we first got our hands on it in 2023.
It promptly changed the rulebook on how drivers interact with electric cars. Its N e-Shift system is universally lauded, and the 5 N won the 2024 Performance Car of the Year award, among other accolades.
Although officially classified as an SUV, the raised hatchback didn't always scream mega performance to me. Don't get me wrong: it delivered the searing acceleration, responsive handling, and everyday usability Hyundai's N division is built on, but I felt there was more to extract from the formula.
Enter the IONIQ 6 N , a mid-sized fastback saloon with a lower roll centre and stiffer spring rates. This strikingly sporty-looking performance car retains the 5 N’s agility and improves handling with a lower roofline and revised suspension geometry.
The 6 N gets upgraded cooling hardware and smarter battery thermal management software. It also gets an upgraded N Drift Optimiser with multi-stage adjustment to fine-tune your slidy sessions.
The IONIQ 6 N seems like the car for anyone serious about the unserious side of motoring. Want to have fun shredding your 275-section Pirelli P Zero tyres, lock in for some hot laps, or ferry the kids to school? You can.
Photo: Naveed Hussain / autoevolution At its core, the recipe is the same as its boxy sibling. An 84kWh battery powers a pair of motors that produce 601bhp and 770Nm, with a rear bias. If that isn’t enough, and I don’t see how it wouldn’t be, then an extra 40bhp can be unlocked for ten seconds using the unmistakably bright red NGB button on the steering wheel.
Despite the same internals, the 6 N claims to reach 62mph in just 3.2 seconds. That’s two tenths faster than the 5 N. The banana-shaped body and sloping rear end, however divisive, help it slice through the air.
The initial hit of torque feels like most other electric cars, but very quickly you discover it isn’t. Partly because of the 50kg reduction in weight over the 5 N, and partly because the motors respond to inputs more quickly. There’s significant pulling power to thrust the weight in a way that doesn’t make sense.
Preparation is required because the 6 N can accumulate speed so quickly. The firm seats support you as you're pushed into them, followed by the all-too-familiar stomach-drop feeling. Long straights feel short, and you'll need to brake sooner than you think because the four-piston brakes (by wire) blend with regen, making pedal input difficult to predict.
Around corners, the 6 N holds the road with confidence, but cycle through the various N mode menus, and the level of grip and wheelspin can be adjusted. Keep everything in the default ‘high grip’ setting, and the driven front wheels hold the road at turn-in, with bags of torque at the rear end to make light work of corner exit.
Hyundai's N e-Shift is present in the 6 N and is addictively fun to use. The simulated 8-speed gear ratios are now even shorter, encouraging you to stay in lower gears for longer. The sound, albeit artificial, sounds somewhat convincingly like a growly V6 and even features crackles.
​ Photo: Naveed Hussain / autoevolution It's fantastic with the flappy paddles, and knowing you're not burning any more fuel in lower gears makes it more satisfying. I use it as often as I can, especially when carrying passengers, because the sound and gear shifts help alleviate any symptoms of motion sickness.
The steering wheel is pleasingly weighty, though feedback is infrequent, and body roll is kept to a minimum. Compared to the taller 5 N, it is more relaxed when pushed hard mid-corner. Though at lower speed, like in a tight car park, I'd much prefer the shorter crossover SUV.
The 6 N has a nice level of comfort and balance that its boxy sibling can't match. The 15mm longer wheelbase improves the ride over speed bumps making the 6 N a nicer car to drive on poorer roads. It's not perfect, but it's impressive considering how polarising the 6 N’s personality can be between rampant and relaxed.
The 6 N’s wheels are smaller than the 5 N’s at only 20 inches, and that dramatic swan-neck spoiler adds 96kg of downforce. I imagine these are mostly to improve efficiency rather than provide comfort or increase performance. The claimed WLTP range is just over 300 miles, but can be significantly slashed in cold weather and with a heavy right foot.
Driving efficiency swings between 2 and 3 kWh, but employ a bit of frugal driving and it'll return almost 4 kWh. Easier said than done because the temptation to drive like a racing driver on a qualifying lap is all too frequent. Keep the 6 N in a gentle cruise and you're rewarded with a smooth, refreshing journey.
The 6 N adopts an all-round calmer character on motorways. It glides along with only the slightest hint of motor whine, only being upset by extreme changes in the road surface. Charging on the go using the 800V architecture means a 10-80% charge in 18 minutes on a 350kW DC charger, or 25 minutes on a 150kW DC charger.
​ Photo: Naveed Hussain / autoevolution The cabin feels a bit busy, but I'm not opposed to having physical buttons for infotainment controls. It's a shame the climate control uses touch technology despite sitting in a separate dedicated bank on the dashboard. The steering wheel also features plenty of buttons, including two customisable N buttons which are handy when you want to apply a specific driving profile.
And that's important to note: there are so many ways to adjust the driving dynamics of the IONIQ 6 N that you'll never tire of it. All the way from responsible Eco mode to the clinical prowess of sport mode, and when you're bored of your tyres you can shred them with varying levels of drift angle and wheelspin.
The key thing is that Hyundai has built a car that is more pleasant to use daily, but also fiercer than the 5 N. It hasn't traded rowdiness for comfort; it has elevated its performance to extract a broader spectrum of ability. It can be calm, composed and thrilling. If the IONIQ 5 N changed the game, the 6 N has taken things to another level.

This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla’s latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in , and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark.
Huawei believes its new Luterra S2 is more than just a home backup battery. The Chinese tech firm is calling it an “all-in-one residential energy system” that combines a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, and AI-powered energy management in a single, simple, and stackable package that’s available in single-phase versions that put out between 3 and 10 kW and three-phase versions that can push up to 20 kW.
The Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei’s proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It’s so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes.
“We are thrilled to introduce Huawei Luterra S2, our next-generation all-in-one residential energy system,” said Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV & BESS Business. “By combining full-SiC architecture, AI-driven energy management, and industry-leading safety, Luterra S2 is designed to be smaller, lighter, quieter, safer, smarter and more powerful than ever before.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
All about the all in one
Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV and BESS.
Huawei’s basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with “just” 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That’s enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you’ll want to keep going if you’re preparing for more than a day or two without power.
If that sounds like you, Luterra’s got you covered. T he modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems , with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel.
Keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB ( about the same as my Mac mini ). It operates at ambient temperatures from –25° C to about 60° C, and features a sturdy IP66-rated enclosure (safe to hit with a high-pressure hose) with corrosion protection up to C5-M to keep it from rusting away.
Alas, the Luterra S2 probably won’t be making its way to the US anytime soon – but fear not! If you’re shopping for a Tesla Powerwall alternative that won’t help fund the absolute worst people in politics, there are a number of great home battery systems on the market that can deliver backup power, store your solar energy, and keep your home running when the grid goes down. We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking , and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ new patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.
Originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No. 12,779,916 for its electric tow dolly on 03NOV2026. The patent covers a machine that’s designed to shoulder the trailer’s hitch load with its own ball hitch or fifth-wheel plate, using an on-board electric motor and battery to get the trailer going while its regenerative braking system and AI-backed steering and traction control system keeps everything pointed in the right direction.
In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a big tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction. The vehicle up front doesn’t necessarily need a massive motor, heavy-duty suspension or oversized brakes. With a system like this, you could argue that the “tow vehicle” isn’t really a tow vehicle at all. It’s more of a “lead vehicle,” since the dolly is the one doing the towing … and it can follow just about anything – including the diminutive ( and supremely affordable ) Fiat 500e, which is also made by Stellantis .
What is actually in the patent
To be clear, this isn’t just Uncle Jojo making fun of the commuter conveys – Stellantis’ patent describes the dolly as being equipped with an autonomous control system using cameras, sensors, a controller, and an advanced, four wheel steer-by-wire system. It also specifically discusses how the dolly’s independently powered acceleration, braking and steering, and sway controls essentially remove the need to own a truck in the first place.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The dolly system’s truck bed sides and small size allow users to experience the functionality and utility of a truck only when they need it, allowing them to own a smaller, cheaper, and more fuel efficient vehicle that suits daily use needs. US PATENT No .
There are some pretty obvious practical questions still to answer, of course, including how much battery capacity the dolly would need, how much weight it could handle and how it would perform on long grades or in emergency braking situations. And, to be clear, a patent isn’t a product announcement or proof that Stellantis plans to put one of these things on sale – heck, if I were Stellantis’ CEO, I’d patent this thing just to prevent anyone else from building one so I could keep selling ancient, low-tech, high-margin Ram Trucks – but it’s a neat idea.
I think it’s neat, anyway. What do you guys think? Are you ready to trade in your big-battery Chevy Silverado EV or Volvo VNR 800 on a new Topolino , or are you going to keep driving inefficient 99% of the time? Let us know, in the comments.

EICMA 2026 • Benelli Showed the World Its New Tornado Naked Tre 903 Concept at EICMA 2026 and It's a Triple!
A "Bijou Luxury Apartment" on Wheels: The 2027 Coachman Laser 855 Xtra Is All That, and More
32 photos
Photo: Coachman Caravans
A travel trailer that's "unashamedly spacious," with "no compromises" and features than are even better than what you have at home, that's how Coachman Caravans describes the Laser 855 Xtra. That's a bold move that sets the bar very high, but the 855 delivers.
Coachman Caravans is the leading UK manufacturer of premium touring caravans, with a history going back to the mid-1980s. The Laser series, which debuted originally in the late '90s, was refreshed in 2020, earning the Xtra moniker and the extra width – becoming in the process the first travel trailer in the UK to be offered on a widebody chassis.
The Laser series is comprised of six floorplans for 2027, any one of them "built to elevate every journey." This description, along with those in that first paragraph, should tell you that the Laser Xtra caravans are "xtra" beyond their extra width: they're premium products that aim to rival the style and comfort of an actual home. Coachman is positive they even surpass it.
The 855 is the mid-entry floorplan, so it's a neat blend of the extra luxuriousness of the bigger models and the relative compactness of smaller ones. It offers sleeping for as many as four people at once, but it seems to have been designed with a traveling couple in mind first and foremost.
Photo: Coachman Caravans As a couple's caravan, it's very spacious, very well appointed, and almost impossibly beautiful. It is, in short, just the kind of caravan you want to retire to after an exhausting day out and about, but it is also made to live exclusively on campgrounds.
The Laser 855 Xtra sits on a premium AL-KO chassis and comes in at 7.89 meters (25.11 feet) in length and 2.4 meters (8 feet) in width. It rides on a tandem axle, which means it's among the Laser floorplans that have a bit more payload than the single-axle variants.
The layout puts a spacious, L-shaped lounge at the front of the trailer and the bedroom at the rear, with a pass-through kitchen on the campside and a pass-through bathroom that doubles as extra privacy buffer for the bedroom, in case you do decide to take two more travelers with you.
Photo: Coachman Caravans They will be sleeping in living room, where the sofa converts into a comfy double bed by means of a slatted extension you pull out manually.
During the day, the L-shaped seating area offers space to move around or, conversely, the perfect spot to relax in front of the TV – assuming you splurge on it, since it's not included in the standard package. European caravan makers operate following a different understanding of the term "luxury" than U.S. counterparts, and it rules out features like AC units, TVs, or fireplaces.
The same seating area will double as a dining space , with help from a collapsible table that tucks into a dedicated compartment.
Photo: Coachman Caravans The galley kitchen is compact but nicely appointed, with a four-burner hybrid gas-electric cooktop, a large oven and grill, a separate microwave, an extractor, and a large fridge with freezer across the way. The L-shaped design allows for plenty of prep space, a large sink with a cover, and maximized storage, but as you will see in the video tour at the bottom of the page, Coachman is also delivering in terms of visual appeal.
Composite counters, real wood cabinetry with concave faces and elegant hardware, and accent lighting throughout create a true "apartment on wheels" vibe. The sense of space is also unprecedented for a European travel trailer, both because of the extra width and the thoughtful design.
The bathroom is pass-through, just like the kitchen , but you have the possibility to close off both doors at its ends and convert it into a single room. On the off-side, you have the toilet (a cassette toilet, as is customary), a heated towel rack, and a raised bowl on a beautiful vanity. Across the way is the step-in shower, with black hardware and double glass doors.
Photo: Coachman Caravans Then, there's the bedroom, imagined as a private oasis with everything you'd need. It features an island bed with a tilting head (the European version of the Versa-Tilt used in the U.S., but manual), matching wardrobes on either side, a padded headboard, acoustic walls in soft-touch textile, and plenty of natural light from all sides.
New for 2027 to the Laser 855 Xtra are five-spoke alloy wheels, full-length exterior graphics, the black radiator in the bathroom, and the 12V Nevada multi-function panel. Standard features still include AL-KO stabilizers, ATC , Alde heating and endless hot water, and a Scorpion S7 tracker with a one-year subscription included.
Options include a Truma Aventa AC, a 120W Truma flexible solar panel, and the option to uprate the chassis to carry more payload.
Photo: Coachman Caravans In standard spec, you're looking at an empty weight of 1,780 kg (3,924 lbs), with a maximum permissible weight of 1,940 kg (4,277 lbs). That's not leaving you with much payload capacity, but it's standard for the caravan segment in Europe.
Dealers are listing the 2027 Laser 855 Xtra for an OTR (On the Road) price of £46,220. That's approximately €55,400 or $61,000 at the current exchange rate, but takes these figures as a reference only. Coachman Caravans doesn't ship internationally, so these gorgeous caravans are out of reach.

EICMA 2026 • Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
Miracle on the Mississippi: Cruiser Topples and Sinks After Being Hit by Tanker, Everyone's OK
13 photos
Photo: YouTube/ABC News
Of all the ways in which 150 people imagined a few days of cruising up and down the Mississippi would go, this was not it. American Heritage, a cruise ship from American Cruise Lines, capsized after being rammed into by a seemingly out of control tanker.
The incident unfolded at midday on Friday, November 13, when the American Heritage cruiser was docked at the Port of New Orleans. Documents cited by local media note that the riverboat had been tied up in the same position for two hours and was just letting passengers off, when the collision occurred.
Atlantic Asphalt, a tanker carrying asphalt owned by Chinese and Liberian companies but flagged in the Marshall Islands, crossed under the bridge and headed directly towards the cruiser , hitting it in the center of the hull. Even though the tanker had dropped anchor in the hope of slowing down, the impact was forceful enough to roll the riverboat over almost instantly.
The cruiser toppled and started to sink, as passengers were either thrown or jumped into the water. American Heritage has a 150-guest boarding capacity, but reports note that there were 200 people onboard, including crew members.
Photo: YouTube/ABC News All these people have since been accounted for, but 32 have been hospitalized for mild injuries. In a statement to the media, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno has called this "a miracle on the Mississippi," given the force of the impact . She thanked all partners and first-responders for making said miracle happen.
An investigation is now underway to determine the cause of the accident. First reports indicate that the tanker had an issue with steering, which prevented the captain from stopping or redirecting the vessel to prevent the collision. One of the guests on the cruiser told the media that crew on the tanker were "running around like ants" right before the moment of impact.
The American Heritage was a paddlewheeler built in 2015, part of the American Cruise Lines fleet. It was a five-deck vessel with a glass-enclosed restaurant, open-seat dining, and three guest lounges, as well as gorgeous accommodation and style "celebrating the Mighty Mississippi River."
Photo: American Cruise Lines It had left New Orleans on a multi-day cruise to Vicksburg and back, traveling at maximum capacity.
Reports say the tanker smashed into the glass restaurant, with the bow piercing a gaping hole into it, through which water rushed in. It was a scene "like in the [movie] Titanic," one guest says, with the impact so powerful as to throw her across on the floor.
Photo: YouTube/ABC News Mayor Moreno says that guests are being offered support for accommodation, transport, and medicine. While the worst has passed, the situation is still unfolding.
